global: Ser {player} has bested me for the third time. Mark this day, for my patience is spent and my blade grows restless.
Three defeats at the hands of ser {player}. The ancestors weep, and I begin to suspect they are laughing.
Once is misfortune, twice is a pattern, and thrice is a rivalry I will end. Ser {player}, I am coming for you.
Ser {player} wins yet again. I shall not forget the grin that followed, nor the pride I was made to swallow.
Ser {player} has now beaten me three times. I have begun to suspect witchcraft in their footwork. I shall investigate.
Ser {player} dares to take my honour thrice? My {troop_count} banners will remember, and so will your grave.
Another defeat at ser {player}'s hand. I am weary of the loss, yet the sting of it will not let me rest.
A soul learns more from three losses than from one victory, they say. Ser {player}, I have learned enough to beat you.
whisper: Ser {player}, you have humbled me thrice now. Enjoy it while the taste is sweet, for I will have my revenge.
Thrice you have stood over me, ser {player}. I swear by my house that the fourth time will be different.
I have counted your victories, ser {player}, and I am tired of the sum. Meet me again if you dare.
Do you find it amusing to beat me, ser {player}? I find it a stain on my name and I intend to wash it clean.
Your third win over me still burns, ser {player}. Keep your smug silence, for it will not last long.
A grudge is a patient thing, ser {player}. Mine has grown fat on your victories and now it wants blood.
Each defeat at your hand is a stone in my boot, ser {player}. I will walk on it until I can remove it.
Do not mistake my silence for surrender, ser {player}. Three losses have only sharpened my resolve.

global: Ser {player} has now prevailed three times over the same rival. A curious pattern, worth a thoughtful look in the realm's records.
The contest with ser {player} is becoming a habit. Habits are dangerous things, friends, so I will mind it closely.
Ser {player} keeps the better hand these days. I take it as a fact of this season, nothing more, nothing less.
Another loss to ser {player}, and I find I merely nod. Some storms are simply the weather of the road.
The third time ser {player} has bested me. I will spend no more breath on it, and will spend my time on the road instead.
Ser {player} has shown skill beyond the usual. Whether it is luck or fate, the ancestors alone can say.
Ser {player} has won again. I shall not make a song of it, though the tavern will likely make one for me.
I have lost to ser {player} three times now. Let the matter rest until we meet again, and let the tally stand as it is.
whisper: Ser {player}, you have bested me thrice now. I bear no grudge, yet I would like to know what you did differently.
It seems our paths keep crossing in contest, ser {player}. I am content to let the outcome stand for now.
Three times you have had the better of me, ser {player}. I am not angry, only curious how you read my guard.
Ser {player}, I doubt my pride will recover soon. Still, I would welcome a fair meeting once my wounds are healed.
Ser {player}, your skill is considerable. I shall keep my distance and my wits about me when we next meet.
Three losses to you, ser {player}. Let us call the tally fair and speak of other matters.
Ser {player}, I am not sure whether to thank you for the lessons or curse you for the bruises. Perhaps both.
Three defeats, ser {player}. I have no complaint about the rules of the field, only about my own footing.

global: Ser {player} has beaten me three times and still I call them my truest rival. Let all Ormerath hear the praise.
Thrice ser {player} has bested me, and thrice I have bowed with a smile. Honour in defeat is its own kind of victory.
Ser {player} wins again, and the field grows brighter for it. Friends, learn from this noble opponent.
Three falls before ser {player}, and I count each one as a lesson gladly taken. Long may our contests continue.
I have lost to ser {player} thrice and would lose a fourth time gladly, for the company of a worthy foe is rare.
Ser {player} has humbled me again. Let the minstrels sing of the fine contest, and of the fine foe who won it.
Ser {player} has beaten me three times, and the ancestors would be proud of such a gracious winner.
A third loss to ser {player}. I will boast of it at every table, for to be defeated by such a champion is no shame.
whisper: Ser {player}, thrice you have bested me. My pride is bruised, but my respect is doubled. Shall we meet again?
You have beaten me three times now, ser {player}. Come and meet me again, and I will bring better wine this time.
Ser {player}, I am glad to lose to you. Your victories keep me sharp, and that is a gift I value.
Three falls, ser {player}, and still I would ride beside you. Friends who test each other are the rarest kind.
Ser {player}, you have my sword's respect and my admiration. I will challenge you again whenever you wish.
Well fought again, ser {player}. Next time I will try a bolder line, though I doubt it will save me from you.
Ser {player}, your third win has me laughing rather than sulking. Let us have a drink and plan the fourth.
Thrice defeated by ser {player}, and never once ashamed. I hope our paths cross often on the road ahead.
